title: The First Three Forms
subtitle: Effect Glowing, Simple Sauna, Kinetic Shove, and the rush that followed
summary: The first practical spell, Effect Glowing, was demonstrated with markings painted on the wrists and published as a scientific paper. It became major news and started a rush. Within a short time Simple Sauna and Kinetic Shove proved that spellcasting could be reproduced, rediscovered and built upon.
content:
> *"Researchers already knew the Gates could make things glow. What they did not know was that a person could make something glow, on purpose, and then write down how."*
> — from a University of Verna lecture on the history of spellcasting

Every caster in Endros learns three names early: **Effect Glowing**, **Simple Sauna** and **Kinetic Shove**. They were the first three **Forms**, learned techniques that use a magical Word to produce a defined effect, and between them they turned a scattering of strange laboratory results into a field of science.

They came before anyone understood Words, and well before anyone could manifest one without a Rune. How Runes were studied before them is in [[runes-of-the-gates|Runes]]; what was learned by comparing them afterwards is in [[the-vocabulary-breakthrough|The Vocabulary Breakthrough]].

## Effect Glowing

**Effect Glowing** was the first practical First Form ever demonstrated. It uses the Word `Glow`, and it does one thing: it makes an object shed light and glow.

Its discoverer was Professor [Manhattan R. Wylde](characters.html#manhattan-wylde) of the [[university-of-verna|University of Verna]], the doctoral supervisor of [Palava Bansz](characters.html#palava-bansz-2), who is now one of his doctoral candidates. The title and date of the paper are not recorded in this entry.

The original technique was awkward. The caster **painted particular runic markings on the wrists**, performed a sequence of motions, and did all of it while a suitable source of magic, in practice a Rune, was present. Done correctly, the object glowed. The size of the object changed how it looked: a large object spread the light across more material and seemed dimmer, while a very small one could shine extraordinarily brightly. The example everyone remembers is a **small pearl**, made exceptionally bright.

> **How the demonstration is usually told in Endros (a retelling, not a record)**
>
> Professor Wylde rolled back his sleeves, showed his painted wrists to the room, and set a single pearl on a black cloth in the middle of the table.
>
> "Note," he said, "that the Rune is on the far side of the bench. I am not touching it."
>
> Nothing happened for long enough that someone at the back began, politely, to cough. Then the pearl lit: first a glint, then a point, then a light so bright that half the audience looked away and the other half forgot to.
>
> "Again," said someone.
>
> He did it again.

The breakthrough was not that something glowed. Gate artifacts had been doing impossible things for years. The breakthrough was **repetition**: a human being had demonstrated a technique that deliberately produced a magical effect, every time it was performed correctly, and could explain the procedure well enough for others to try it. That is the moment most historians of the field treat as the birth of practical spellcasting.

## The Paper and the Rush

He wrote the method up and **published it** as a scientific paper. It became major news, well beyond academic circles.

What followed felt like a gold rush. Universities, laboratories, private researchers, artificers, industrial concerns, governments and their military offices, wealthy patrons, engineers and Expeditioners all wanted to be the next to find a Form. Anyone with access to a Rune and a bench was, briefly, a potential pioneer.

> **From a mainland newspaper, the week the paper appeared (excerpt)**
>
> *LIGHT FROM NOTHING. Scholar Makes a Pearl Burn Like a Lamp, and Tells the World How. "It Can Be Repeated," Professor Wylde Insists.*
>
> *Our correspondent asked whether the method could be learned by an ordinary person. Professor Wylde replied that it could be learned by anyone with patience, a steady hand and access to a Rune, "which is to say, at present, almost nobody."*

## Simple Sauna

**Simple Sauna** was announced soon afterwards. It uses the Word `Heat`, and it heats up a room or a local area.

Its original technique centred on a **symbol drawn on the floor**, with the effect arranged around the marked area. It came from a **Vardic research team** working in the University of Verna's research facilities in Endros, and it was not simply derived from the Effect Glowing paper. That mattered more than the warmth. A second team, working its own way, had found a different repeatable Form. Spellcasting was not one professor's trick. It was a discipline that more than one group could discover independently.

The team's approach was recognisably Vardic: less interested in why the effect worked than in whether it worked every time, and what it was good for (see [[iron-timber-and-names|Iron, Timber and Names]]).

> **In a University laboratory in Endros, as a Vernan colleague remembered it**
>
> "Why the floor?" asked the Vernan. "The Glowing paper puts its markings on the wrists."
>
> "Because that's where the room is," said the Vard, chalking the last line of the symbol. "We wanted a warm room."
>
> "And the symbol? Where does it come from?"
>
> "Trial forty-one." She stood up and dusted off her knees. "The first forty didn't work. Write that down too, if you're writing things down."

## Kinetic Shove

**Kinetic Shove** followed. It uses the Word `Move` and forcefully shoves a target, suddenly giving it motion; accounts of early demonstrations speak of objects knocked across a room at something like ten metres a second.

Kinetic Shove was developed using **the methodology established in the Effect Glowing paper**. Its discoverers took a published method, applied it to a different effect, and got a new result. It is one of the first examples of one magical discovery deliberately building on another, and it is usually taken as the moment spellcasting stopped being a run of lucky finds and became a **research field**.

## Why Three Was Enough

One Form is a curiosity. Three, from different hands and in quick succession, are a pattern:

- **Effect Glowing** proved that magic could be manipulated deliberately and repeatably by a human technique.
- **Simple Sauna** proved that others could discover Forms independently.
- **Kinetic Shove** proved that published work could be built upon.

Together they made the next step inevitable: someone had to compare them, Rune by Rune and mark by mark, and ask what they had in common.

## The Forms Today

All three are still taught, and all three still show their age. Their original procedures carry steps that may not be needed. The wrist markings of Effect Glowing in particular are widely expected to prove unnecessary once the Form is better understood; nobody has yet published the proof. Each of the three is recorded in [Discoveries](discoveries.html#forms), and how Forms work in play is on the Rules page: [Forms](game.html#post-forms).
